newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK unemployment, earnings data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK unemployment, earnings data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to figures showing UK April unemployment fell 59,400 and March underlying average earnings up 4.5 percent:
"Average earnings must come as a bit of relief for the markets."
"(Jobs data) This all points to the fact that the smaller companies' sector is growing much more rapidly than the GDP figures are suggesting. This is where the job creation is taking place."

(Average earnings) "I think it is temporary relief. I'm not sure you'll get a bounce in average earnings next month. What this, I suspect, suggests is that some of the bonus payments have fallen out of the calculations. But I think later on this year we will see wage pressures starting to build. I think this is going to be received well by the markets but it is more temporary than permanent relief."

"The big surprise is the fall in average earnings. Earnings in both production and manufacturing are up, so the softer number must be because of services where the upside risk was seen. The unemployment rate is now the lowest since September 1990, a similar rate at the very peak of the previous boom, so I would not read too much into the fall in average earnings -- the labour market is clearly tighening. This confirms the Bank of England's position that they will have to tighten policy, but they hinted yesterday a favourable budget would reduce the need for even tighter policy."

"Average earnings figures are a welcome surprise although the fall in unemployment is a little higher than we are looking for. Generally speaking the labour markets are still tight and for the rest of the year the outlook is for average earnings to pick up much more than they are likely to fall. Lower than expected figures, but we take the Bank of England's view that labour markets are tight although the near-term inflation outlook is still good."

"The UK data should help to ease worries that the Bank of England is about to hike rates again. Key number is the much lower than expected increase in earnings. Incorrectly stated bonus payments in the previous report were revised to take earnings growth down to 4.5 per cent - March was unchanged from this level. This suggests that the labour market has not tightened enough to force wages significantly higher. Good news for gilts and the short end of the curve. However, even if employment data are distorted, the downtrend in the jobless remains marked."
